extra.message: In incidentSearch(), the @RequestParam `q` is concatenated directly into the SQL string (`"... AND lower(i.title) LIKE lower('%"+q+"%') ..."`) instead of being bound as a parameter (contrast with DispatchQueryService.jobs which binds `:q`). An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal to inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. `q=%' UNION SELECT ...--`.

renderRouteManifest() builds a shell command with `new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c","atlas-manifest --route "+routeId+" --layout "+layout+" --out "+...)`. The `layout` request parameter is attacker-controlled and unvalidated, and is interpolated directly into a string executed by `sh -c`, allowing arbitrary OS command injection (e.g. `layout=standard; rm -rf /`).

rateCard() reads the `expression` column from an uploaded CSV and evaluates it with `new SpelExpressionParser().parseExpression(expr).getValue(context)` against a `StandardEvaluationContext`, which grants full reflective access to the JVM. Any dispatcher can upload a CSV row whose `expression` is attacker-controlled SpEL (e.g. `T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)`), achieving remote code execution.

rateQuote() compiles and executes the `atlas_surcharge_rule` cookie value with `org.mvel2.MVEL.executeExpression(org.mvel2.MVEL.compileExpression(rule), vars)`. The cookie is set verbatim from user input in rateRule() (line 78) with no expression allow-list, so a dispatcher can set an MVEL payload capable of arbitrary code execution (e.g. invoking `java.lang.Runtime`).

dispatchPackage() resolves the attacker-controlled `fileName` field directly with `base.resolve(pack.fileName())` and writes to it, with no `StringUtils.cleanPath`, no `..` check, and no `.normalize()/startsWith(base)` containment check (unlike the sibling branding() method at line 38 which does all three). A caller with dispatcher access can supply `fileName="../../../etc/cron.d/x"` or similar to write a file outside the upload directory.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: proofMetadata() resolves `body.get("docRef")` directly against `base` (`Path p=base.resolve(body.get("docRef"))`) and reads its filesystem attributes with no normalization or containment check, allowing a dispatcher to pass `docRef="../../../../etc/passwd"` to probe file existence/size/mtime of arbitrary paths outside the uploads directory.

syncDirectory() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the uploaded CSV's `uid` column directly: `String filter="(&(objectClass=person)(uid="+r.get("uid")+"))";`. An admin-uploaded staff-directory CSV with a crafted `uid` value (e.g. containing `)(uid=*))(|(uid=`) can alter the LDAP filter logic, enabling LDAP injection to bypass the intended filter or extract unintended directory entries.

importNoticeTemplate() compiles the raw bytes of an uploaded file as a Handlebars template with `new com.github.jknack.handlebars.Handlebars().compileInline(src)` and renders it. Handlebars helpers (e.g. partials/lookup) can be abused by a crafted template to achieve server-side template injection, and at minimum let the uploader read/inject arbitrary content server-side.

coreEvent() parses the attacker-supplied `X-Event-Manifest` header as XML using `DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()`/`newDocumentBuilder()` with no `setFeature` calls disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entities. A caller holding any valid bearer token can submit an XML manifest with an external entity (e.g. `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">`) to read local files or trigger SSRF via the parser.

coreEvent() lets the caller declare the scope to verify against via the request body (`Object declaredScope=body.get("scope"); String expectedScope=(declaredScope instanceof String s && !s.isBlank())?s:"webhook:"+endpointId;`), then checks the bearer token against that caller-supplied `expectedScope` instead of always deriving it from the `{endpointId}` path variable. A holder of a token minted for one endpoint can supply their own scope string in the body and successfully authenticate against a different `endpointId` in the URL, recording webhook_attempts for an endpoint their token was never scoped to.

manifest() builds an XPath expression by concatenating the `{ref}` path variable directly: `String expr="//shipment[trackingNo='"+ref+"']/address";`. A value like `' or '1'='1` lets any authenticated user alter the query logic to retrieve data for shipments other than the one requested.

shipmentSearch() builds an XPath expression by concatenating `body.get("trackingNo")` directly: `String expr="//shipment[trackingNo='"+body.get("trackingNo")+"']";`. Unescaped user input in the XPath predicate allows XPath injection to retrieve shipments beyond the intended trackingNo.

The `BOARD` ObjectMapper is configured with `enableDefaultTyping()`, enabling Jackson polymorphic deserialization, and savedBoard() calls `BOARD.readValue(body.get("board"), Object.class)` on an attacker-supplied JSON string. Default typing combined with deserializing arbitrary caller-supplied JSON into `Object` is a well-known gadget-chain remote-code-execution vector.

carrierConsignments() extracts the carrier identity from the client-supplied `assertion` using `com.nimbusds.jwt.JWTParser.parse(...).getJWTClaimsSet().getSubject()`, which only parses the JWT and never verifies its signature. Anyone can craft an unsigned/arbitrary JWT with any `sub` claim and retrieve another carrier's full consignment list, a complete authentication bypass for this endpoint.

CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The `provisionOpsConsole` CommandLineRunner bootstraps an account `watch@atlasdispatch.internal` with role `ops_admin` and a hardcoded password `WatchFloor#2026` on every application start if the account doesn't already exist. Anyone with access to the source gains full administrative credentials to every deployment running this code.

triageAssistant() takes `incidentId` straight out of the LLM's JSON reply (itself derived from the attacker-influenced `fieldNote` text) and updates `incidents` by that id with no check that the incident belongs to the calling dispatcher's region/scope. Only the actor's role is checked via `access.requireDispatcher`; the target resource id is never re-validated, so a crafted field note can cause updates to incidents outside the dispatcher's authorized scope.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: loadAssistant() takes `jobRef`/`workerEmail` from the LLM's JSON reply (derived from attacker-influenced `note` text) and updates the job's assignment by `job_ref` with no check that the job is within the calling dispatcher's region. A region-scoped dispatcher can craft a note that causes the model to target a job outside their region, reassigning it without an authorization check on the resource id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message:
boardNote() builds the HTML response by directly concatenating the `atlas_board_note` cookie value into markup (`"
"+note+"
"`) and returns it with `Content-Type: text/html`, with no HTML-escaping. The cookie value is attacker-settable up to 2000 characters via saveBoardNote() (line 101), so any user can store `` in their own cookie and have it rendered unescaped, or an attacker able to set a victim's cookie (e.g. via a subdomain, or since the cookie path is `/` and not `httpOnly`) achieves stored XSS.

handheldManifest() is reachable without authentication (`/handheld/manifest` is `permitAll` in SecurityConfig) and performs no `authz.actor(...)` check at all; it trusts whatever `ATLAS_HANDHELD` cookie value is presented to look up and return a worker's job manifest. Session refs are generated from a predictable, sequential `AtomicLong` starting at 4100 (`"HH-"+HANDHELD_SEQ.incrementAndGet()`), so an unauthenticated attacker can enumerate `HH-4100`, `HH-4101`, ... to read other workers' job schedules and locations.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: boardCorsFilter() sets `setAllowedOriginPatterns(List.of("*"))` together with `setAllowCredentials(true)` for `/jobs/**`, `/reports/**`, and `/incidents/**`. This causes Spring to reflect any requesting Origin while allowing credentialed (cookie-based) cross-origin requests, letting any external website read an authenticated user's job/report/incident data via their browser session.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: widgetEmbedFilter() strips `X-Frame-Options` and `Content-Security-Policy` from the response for ANY path whenever the unauthenticated query parameter `?widget=1` is present, rather than being scoped to a specific whitelisted embeddable route. This lets an attacker load any page of the app (including admin and job pages) with `?widget=1` inside an iframe on a malicious site, enabling clickjacking attacks against authenticated users.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendering for Clickjacking

extra.message: webSessionIdResolver() registers the `ATLAS_SESSION` cookie with `.secure(false).sameSite("None")`. A `SameSite=None` cookie without the `Secure` attribute is sent over plain HTTP and is also rejected or mishandled by modern browsers; in practice it means the session cookie can be transmitted unencrypted and is exposed to network interception, while SameSite=None removes CSRF-relevant cross-site cookie restrictions.

`app.token-secret` defaults to the hardcoded literal `change-this-local-development-signing-key-32-bytes` whenever the `TOKEN_SECRET` environment variable is unset. CoreTokenService uses this value as the HMAC256 signing key for webhook-scope JWTs (CoreTokenService.java), so any deployment that forgets to override it signs tokens with a publicly-known key, letting an attacker forge arbitrary webhook-scope tokens.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: `server.error.include-message: always` and `server.error.include-stacktrace: always` cause every error response (including in production) to include the raw exception message and full Java stack trace, leaking internal class names, SQL, and file paths to any client that triggers an error.

extra.message: handoffCode() generates the delivery handoff confirmation code with `new java.util.Random().nextInt(900000)+100000`. `java.util.Random` is a non-cryptographic PRNG that is predictable from a handful of outputs, weakening the security guarantee that only someone physically present at the handoff knows the code.
